pr_title: TSDB: keep duplicate series records in checkpoints while their samples may still be present
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/16058

Renames the head's `deleted` map to `walExpiries`, and creates entries for any duplicate series records encountered during WAL replay, with the expiry set to the highest current WAL segment number. Any subsequent WAL checkpoints will see the duplicate series entry in the `walExpiries` map, and keep the series record until the last WAL segment that could contain its samples is deleted.

Other considerations:
- WBL
  - series records aren't written to the WBL, so there are no duplicates to deal with
- agent mode
  - has its own WAL replay logic that handles duplicate series records differently, and is outside the scope of this PR

issue_context.title: Duplicate series record handling during WAL checkpoint and replay leads to missing samples
issue_context.body:
If a series:
- stops receiving samples 
- is removed from the head during compaction
- starts receiving samples again

it will be given a new series ID, and have a new series record written to the WAL using this new ID. If there has not been a WAL checkpoint created since the series was removed from the head, the WAL will contain series records and samples for the same series referencing two different series IDs.

Consider the following WAL:
- segment 0:
  - series record with labelset `{foo=bar}` with id `1`
  - samples record for series id `1` @ t=1000
- segment 1:
  - series record with labelset `{foo=bar}` with id `2`
  - samples record for series id `2` @ t=2000
- segment 2:
  - samples record for series id `2` @ t=3000

Assume the WAL was truncated to mint=1500 to allow for the second series reference to be created when the sample at t=2000 arrived. When this WAL is replayed:
- the series will be written to the head with id `1`
- the sample @ t=1000 will be skipped because it is before the mint of the head
- the series record with id `2` will be skipped because a series matching its labelset already exists in the head
- the samples @ t=2000 and t=3000 will be written to the head with series id `1`

If we now create a WAL checkpoint (triggered by e.g. a head compaction) over segments 0-1, the WAL will look like:
- checkpoint 1:
  - series record with labelset `{foo=bar}` with id `1`
  - samples record for series id `2` @ t=2000
- segment 2:
  - samples record for series id `2` @ t=3000

Note that the sample records referencing series id `2` still reference it, but the series record for id `2` has been dropped, because it does not appear in the head.

If we replay this new WAL, the samples for series id `2` @ t=2000 and t=3000 will be dropped, because they reference a WAL series record that no longer exists.
comments: For searchability purposes, can you include one or two examples of the symptom, which I think is a log line?

We noticed this because of these log lines during WAL replay:
```
msg="Unknown series references" samples=32548 exemplars=0 histograms=0 metadata=0
```

Note the high count of samples reported with unknown series references.
